ï»¿**COMMENTS**
This composite source straddles the Adriatic Sea just offshore the coast of the southern Marche, between the latitude of the cities of Macerata (to the northwest) and San Benedetto del Tronto (to the southeast), respectively. It is part of the Umbro-Marche Apennines outer offshore thrust. This front is the NE-verging fault system at the eastern border of the Northern Apennines chain, parallel to the Marche coast.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007, CPTI15) show only a sparse intermediate (4.5 < Mw< 5.0) seismicity, besides the 1480 (Mw 4.9, Ascolano) and the 4 September 1987 (Mw 5.1, Porto San Giorgio) earthquakes that have occurred near the center of the area.
The Umbria-Marche region was thoroughly investigated using seismic reflection profiles, and different interpretations of its structural style are available in the literature. The main differences in the interpretation of the structural style of this region are the position of the basal decollement level of the thrusting, and the presence or absence of secondary decollement levels. Some researchers (Bally et al., 1986; Doglioni et al., 1994) indicate the bottom of the Triassic evaporites as the basal decollement level, and propose that a thin-skinned structural style characterize the Paleogene-Neogene evolution of the belt. Other researchers (Barchi et al., 1998; Finetti et al., 2001; Lavecchia et al., 2003) consider that also the upper portion of the magnetic basement was involved in the thrusting, and propose a thick-shinned structural style. In general there is a good agreement among researches (e.g.: Coward et al., 1999; Barchi et al., 1998; Calamita et al., 1994) about the presence of two main decollement levels inside the accretionary prism, the lower coinciding with the bottom of the Triassic evaporites, on which the major thrust ramps originate, and the shallower coinciding with the Marne a Fucoidi or Scaglia Cinerea formation, on which minor thrusts sheet detach.
The deformation style of the Umbria-Marche region is characterized by two main structural levels: 1) a deeper level consisting of deep and broad anticlines deforming the Mesozoic-Paleogene carbonate succession, produced by thrust faults detaching on the Triassic evaporites; and 2) a shallower level made up of small and tight anticlines, found in the axial zones of the major anticlines, and developed in the Neogene foredeep sediments. These last structures show a more complex structural pattern with respect to the deeper ones.
Other geometrical features of this region are: 1) the occurrence of complex thrust trajectories, due to the presence of several potential detachment levels in the sedimentary multilayer; 2) the shorter wavelength of the shallow anticlines; and 3) the disharmony between different structural levels.
Various sources of evidence suggest that the region just onshore is undergoing NE-SW trending contraction, including earthquake focal mechanisms all along the outer front (Frepoli and Amato, 1997), in particular that of the 1987 Porto San Giorgio earthquake (Riguzzi et al., 1989), while borehole breakout data (Montone et al., 2004) illustrated a NW-SE trending minimum stress axis.
The seismicity around this Composite Source is low to intermediate according to historic and instrumental catalogs. A seismic sequence, occurred in 1986-1987, with magnitude between 4 and 5 was reported a few kilometres to the south of this Source, together with an event, occurred in 1907, with magnitude 4.75 to the east of the source (Rovida et al., 2016; CPTI15 catalogue).
